plan: Given the common knowledge of rationality, the optimal bidding strategy converges to bidding slightly above the expected value of the second highest bid. Since values are between 0 and 49, the expected value of the highest of the remaining two bids is approximately (2/3) * 49 = 32.67. To win with high probability, and minimize overpayment, I will bid slightly above this. A bid of $33.00 seems reasonable.

Given the common knowledge of rationality, the optimal strategy converges to bidding your true value. This is because any deviation (bidding higher) risks overpaying, and bidding lower risks losing an item worth more than the bid. Since this is round 1 of 1, and there's no history, I'll bid my true value.

Given the common knowledge of rationality, the optimal bidding strategy converges towards bidding your true value. However, since we only have one round, and values are drawn independently, a slight underbid is reasonable to avoid overpaying. Bidding slightly below my value of $20 allows me to win only if the second highest bid is significantly lower, maximizing potential profit. I will bid $19.5.
